title: Realignment in Asia, 1971
body: Beginning in 1970, Pakistan faced its biggest internal crisis. Its first general election gave a split verdict, and the rulers in West Pakistan refused to accept the Awami League's victory in East Pakistan or its demand for a federation. In early 1971 the Pakistani army arrested Sheikh Mujib-ur Rahman and unleashed a reign of terror, and about 80 lakh refugees fled into India, which extended moral and material support to the freedom struggle in Bangladesh. Pakistan, in turn, received support from the United States and China. The US-China rapprochement that had begun in the late 1960s resulted in a realignment of forces in Asia; in July 1971 Henry Kissinger, adviser to US President Richard Nixon, made a secret visit to China via Pakistan. In August 1971 India signed a 20-year Treaty of Peace and Friendship with the Soviet Union, which assured India of Soviet support if the country faced any attack. Some observers asked whether India could still call itself non-aligned after signing such a treaty.
